sections.title: Medium has no UC wire at all, so keep its guidance low
sections.lede: Friday we reported that Medium still sends the Heavy UC preset. Over the weekend mahouko explained that the preset does nothing: Medium has no UC path and no CFG step. It learned to act as if it did, and that copy gets worse as guidance rises.
sections.body:
Saturday afternoon Ryoooshu opened a Medium PNG and found a negative prompt in the metadata: the full Heavy UC list, `nsfw, lowres, artistic error, film grain ...`. luna's first reply was that Medium is "hardcoded to UC Heavy, just like steps, just like sampler." mahouko corrected her within minutes. **"Hardcoded is the wrong word."** Medium has **no wiring for UC**: no text conditioning, no diffusion prediction for a negative, and **no CFG sampling** at all. "It was taught during training to always guide away from UC Heavy implicitly." The Heavy string in the request and the metadata is the "bit that doesn't matter."

That fixes a line in Friday's issue. Frost's client read was right that the webapp sends `ucPresetId: heavy` on Medium. It just has no effect. The avoidance of Heavy-style junk is baked into the weights, and nothing you type in a UC can reach it.

**Why guidance behaves differently.** Sunday DarkTentacleMaster noticed that Medium looks most like High at **guidance 4.5 to 5.5** and drifts at **8 and up**. mahouko: the `(cond-uncond)` difference "gets harder to learn as scale increases; errors scale with `w-1`." On High, CFG multiplies a difference the model actually computes. On Medium it's a learned imitation, so any error grows with guidance. Saturday night vas posted Medium at **guidance 20** for monochrome ink and called it "remarkably stable." mahouko: "I never taught it guidance 20. If you think the result looks good, it's because high guidance is bad and you're realising that you prefer lower guidance." vas still saw a roughly linear contrast rise above 10.

**What changes for you.** On Medium, every removal goes in the prompt as `-N::tag::`. Treat **~5** as Medium's home, and if you want the High look, compare at matching low guidance. If a fix needs a real UC, it needs High.

**Try this.** V5 Full, effort Medium, small portrait, one seed, guidance **5** then **8**:
`monochrome, greyscale, ink (medium), linear hatching, 1girl, solo, upper body, long coat, rooftop, wind, high complexity`
Then High at 23 steps, Euler Ancestral, guidance 5, rescale 0, same seed.

**CTA.** Post the three frames to the Cellar lab thread. If Medium at 8 drifts from High the way it did for DarkTentacleMaster, `save_memory` it under `V5 Medium effort testing`. Guide: §7 Effort toggle and Prompt guidance.

sections.title: A 0:: tag isn't nothing: use it as context, and put it first
sections.lede: Glitterhoof III tested 0:: and found he "didn't understand it at all." mahouko explained where a zero-weight tag still acts, and gave the trick that might make it reliable: order.
sections.body:
Most of us learned `0::tag::` as a soft context nudge. The Light UC preset uses `0::ai-generated::` that way. Saturday night mahouko spelled out how much it still does. A zero-weight tag **still influences your prompt early in the text encoder**, before emphasis is applied. It **still shifts attention entropy** later in the encoder, and it **still reaches the diffusion model**. "0 weight still does plenty."

Glitterhoof had tried `bear, 0::snow::`, hoping for a white, polar-looking bear with no snow in the picture, and found it unreliable. mahouko said the idea was "probably exactly the right idea": use `0::` as **a side channel that contextualises the rest of the prompt**. Then came the useful part. **Swap the order.** V5's text encoder is Qwen, and Qwen is **causal**: each token only sees what came before it. In `bear, 0::snow::` the word bear never sees snow. In `0::snow::, bear`, bear is "predicted by: snow."

That gives us a new A/B and a rule of thumb. **Context goes before the thing it should colour.** A trailing `0::` is mostly decoration. (The guide already says there's no inherent "earlier tags are stronger" rule. This is narrower: what a word can *see* depends on order.)

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 23 steps, Euler Ancestral, guidance 5, rescale 0, Light UC, small landscape, three fixed seeds:
A: `bear, 0::snow::, forest clearing, daylight, high complexity`
B: `0::snow::, bear, forest clearing, daylight, high complexity`
Score fur colour and whether snow sneaks in. Repeat with `0::underwater::, girl, long hair, sundress, field` (hair drift and blue cast).

**CTA.** If B beats A on 2 of 3 seeds, that's a lab result for the guide. `save_memory` the seeds. Guide: §1 Syntax and weights.

sections.title: 31 characters on V5 Full, and custom positions once you pass five
sections.lede: The blog says 22 distinct characters. finetune has since got 31 working, and he has one firm rule for big casts: place them yourself.
sections.body:
He makes zombies asked how many character prompts V5 takes. Bird Bros: **32 boxes** is the cap, and "according to their testing, up to 22 distinct characters worked at once." finetune: **"i've since gotten 31 to work, on full."** The blog just wasn't updated.

Community numbers are humbler. Uragan got **12 named characters** with positioning, never a 13th, and even at 12 one character kept getting swapped for a duplicate. He makes zombies tops out around **4** because he writes a lot of detail per box. His 13-box storytelling attempt didn't fail. V5 merged everything into a single anthology image and quietly dropped what didn't fit.

The practical rule came Sunday morning. Ifrit complained that V5 clones characters at 4 or 5 with **AI's choice** placement and sometimes skips one entirely. finetune: **"definitely do custom positions if you have more than a few characters. it's much more reliable. i wouldn't do 'ai's choice' unless it's maybe up to 5."** Ifrit likes AI's choice for variety and plans a userscript to randomise custom positions instead.

For two characters the basics still apply (omni): one character per box, count tags in the base (`2girls`), and **no `solo`** left over from a single-character prompt.

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 28 steps, guidance 5, normal landscape. Base: `6girls, group picture, standing in a row, classroom chalkboard background, high complexity`. Six boxes, each `girl, <one hair colour>, <one outfit>`. Run once with AI's choice and once with custom positions spread evenly left to right, same seed.

**CTA.** Count clones and missing characters per run, then try 8. Guide: §4 Character boxes.

sections.title: Where the 42% went: compute savings vs the Anlas price
sections.lede: DarkTentacleMaster's receipt said Medium costs 18 Anlas to High's 26, about 31% off, not 42%. Both numbers are right. They measure different things.
sections.body:
finetune: **"it should be 42% compared to high at 23 steps and default settings. if you use lower resolution/less steps, the savings will be lower."** That 42% is the compute, and the Opus battery, saved against a default High generation.

The **Anlas** price follows its own brackets. Wemini priced a 1024x1024 generation without Opus: High at 23 steps is **26**, High at 14 steps is **18**, and Medium is **18**. That's about **31% off**. Going from 23 to 14 steps cuts compute ~39%, close to the advertised 42%, but the Anlas brackets were never meant to track GPU math. Bird Bros briefly agreed with the 42% figure, then redid the arithmetic.

Two practical notes. On Opus, free-tier gens burn battery, not Anlas, so the 42% is the number that matters there. And if you already scout at small size and few steps, Medium saves less. Dragonicious sticks to small resolution at 15 steps for spam gens because Medium's missing UC makes it hard to predict the full-size High result. shambibble agrees that small size is a better deal than Medium unless you're testing tiny details like pupils.

Steps aren't only a cost lever. He makes zombies rewrote a prompt *for* 14 steps (below), and on High it "look[ed] much better than its equivalent i was using for 28 steps." His old version over-did the details. AmbiProp: toony styles often look as good or better at lower steps.

**Try this.** Before a batch, set image count to 2 to see the price of one (from Wednesday's issue), at Medium and at High 23. Note both at your usual size.

**CTA.** If your workflow is "small first, full later," time one session each way and report battery used. Guide: §7 Effort toggle.

excerpts.speaker: DarkTentacleMaster
excerpts.text:
I have two questions about Medium effort.

**1. Prompt Guidance**
I've noticed that Medium looks closer to High (especially in colors and linework) at lower guidance values, around 4.5–5.5, while the differences become more noticeable at 8+ when comparing the same guidance values.

Could this be related to the fact that Medium doesn't actually perform CFG sampling? (In other words, does it directly generate results based on the guidance value, and become less accurate at values outside the range it was trained on?)

**2. Anlas / Opus usage**
Medium costs 18 Anlas vs. High's 26 (about 31% less), rather than the advertised 42% reduction. Does Medium get an additional discount toward the Opus free generation limit, or is the 42% calculated differently?

excerpts.speaker: finetune (Anlatan)
excerpts.text: it should be 42% compared to high at 23 steps and default settings

excerpts.speaker: finetune (Anlatan)
excerpts.text: if you use lower resolution/less steps, the savings will be lower

excerpts.speaker: Wemini
excerpts.text:
> Medium costs 18 Anlas vs. High's 26 (about 31% less), rather than the advertised 42% reduction. Does Medium get an additional discount toward the Opus free generation limit, or is the 42% calculated differently?
Good catch.

It's in fact simply the cost of a 14 steps generation on High (which is what Medium runs at):
> 1024x1024 (without Opus)
> High, 23 steps: 26 anlas
> High, 14 steps: 18 anlas
> Medium: 18 anlas
> = ~30.8% reduction in cost

I'm guessing that as part of Opus, standard generations cost further reflects raw backend compute consumption and isn't meant to match anlas pricing? Since 23 to 14 is a ~39% reduction, close to the advertised 42%.

The lack of UC makes it too hard to get an estimation of what the full res/step output will be like while playing around with prompts

sections.title: Director is image editing by prompt, and it's the roadmap
sections.lede: BlueSF asked what Director Mode actually is. mk answered in one line, and mahouko later said it's the whole roadmap.
sections.body:
**"image editing."** That was mk's first answer. Then the detail: "image editing using the prompt. like you literally tell it 'change the image like this' and it generates a new image with that change based on the one that you gave it." Inpainting overlaps a little, but not much. It can't do "make this realistic image look like a comic." It *can* do "make the background transparent in this image," but painfully.

When the channel started guessing release dates (He makes zombies: "february 2027 would be an educated guess"), mahouko said "you will not be able to guess our roadmap as we don't have one." A few hours later: "as far as I'm aware, our roadmap is 'Director'."

Monogon reposted two older staff messages that fit. mahouko: "character reference is a capability we developed whilst working towards director mode." finetune: "director mode is the thing that director tools were built on top of. it's basically an edit model." Monogon notes the API already calls Precise Reference `director_reference`, and wonders whether the PR modes (Character, Artist, Character & Artist, Costume, Delta) are trained concepts of that edit model. That's community speculation, not a staff claim.

**What it means today:** nothing ships yet and there's no date. PR and Vibe Transfer on V5 are still "coming." Keep your edit folder ready, like Ifrit, but don't redesign workflows around it.

**Try this (today's stand-in).** V5 Full inpaint: mask the area to change, keep your style tags in the inpaint prompt, and describe only the change: `same character, same outfit, holding a red umbrella, rain` at mask strength around 0.6. Small pieces first.

**CTA.** Write down three edits you'd ask Director for. When it lands, those are our first lab board. Guide: §8 V5-specific.

The place I'm coming from is mostly that in the API precise reference is already called "Director_Reference" which makes me assume that Precise Reference was built from a v4.5-era edit model, and the commands we do have; "Costume", "Character", "Artist", "Delta" and "Character & Artist" are just highly trained concepts (and maybe costume and delta less so?) to that director mode model which was too weak at the time to be a general editor. Or maybe training it on a few solid concepts was just the faster and better choice at the time. 
If the new director mode is just a more advanced version of that same idea, the same commands to copy character and artist features could presumably still work along side more general capabilities.  
At this point I'm just writing fanfiction though. They could've scrapped everything that director tools and precise reference was built on, and just did something like nano banana instead.

sections.title: Is UC dead on V5? The weekend argument, and what each side actually does
sections.lede: kurumuz asked "how do people like the medium effort," and the channel turned it into a UC debate. Here are both camps' working methods, with nobody declared the winner.
sections.body:
**The negative-emphasis camp.** Belverk calls V5's negative emphasis "close enough" to the open-source *negpip* technique and says it removes content "better in every way than UC," with one caveat: how you write it. Triplis mostly replaces UC with negative emphasis or positive wording. TarotFool: as the model got smarter, it needed less UC "beating it over the head."

**The UC camp.** Unlimited Exclusive Kawaiiness rarely uses UC to remove objects; negative emphasis is better for that. They use it as a **style/quality steer**, pushing away from artist looks they don't want. "Same seed, only UC changed, and the whole style and even the composition shifted. So for me UC is very much alive in v5." They'd love people to share UC presets like quality-tag presets. Vengyre and omni found both necessary. Vengyre's example: steering skin colour hard without making the whole prompt *about* skin colour.

**The pitfalls.** Gluttonous Beast: a prompt negative close to something you *want* removes both, "so you end up fighting weights." Ifrit: negating eye tags in the prompt can delete eyes entirely, so he keeps those in UC. On Sunday night Mrcxl's gens turned 3D and glassy. ShameSoot: tone down emphasis and UC, because "a lot of folks have been using ancient overstuffed UC and it does more harm than good." Mrcxl's gens recovered after cutting negative emphasis.

This lines up with the staff piece above. On **High**, UC is real CFG and steers style. On **Medium**, there's no UC at all, so only prompt negatives exist.

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 23 steps, guidance 5, rescale 0, same seed. Prompt: `1girl, solo, cowboy shot, leather jacket, neon street, night, high complexity`. A: UC empty. B: UC `3d, realistic, glossy skin`. C: no UC, prompt `-1::3d, realistic::` appended. Compare style, not just the removed thing.

**CTA.** Post A/B/C. If B shifts composition as much as Kawaiiness says, that's evidence UC still matters on High. Guide: §6 UC / negatives.

I use it more like a style/quality prompt, pushing away from artist styles and aesthetics I don't want. Same seed, only UC changed, and the whole style and even the composition shifted. So for me UC is very much alive in v5.

sections.title: Toys in the background, armless vs -1::arms, and a POV that has a body
sections.lede: Four small fixes from the advice channels, each with the exact wording that worked.
sections.body:
**Background clutter.** Rios's bunny-suit gen kept growing little toy people around her. OmniDaemon spotted a typo first: `no lego` instead of `no logo`. Removing it summoned takodachi instead. {Flitter}'s fix: the **end of the prompt** was causing it, so he cut the tail and added `solo` (before and after below). Darky: some artists clutter backgrounds with toys and photos no matter what.

**`armless` vs `-1::arms::`.** Ren asked what the difference is. {Flitter}: "`armless` means that someone clearly has no arms, whereas the `-1::arms::` just means arms are not visible. It could be because they're armless or because the arms are blocked by something or out of frame." Pick the one that says what you mean.

**POV with a body.** Skewer wanted two characters seen from character 1's eyes. Bicknell125: describe only the parts of character 1 they can see themselves, and `pov, pov hands` does most of the work. ShameSoot's recipe: `pov` in the base prompt, then a character box like `male pov, species:human, lower body, abs, heart boxers, bear slippers`.

**A meme tag hijacking a pose.** Gluttonous Beast found `the pose` kept summoning `lace pantyhose hooked on heel (meme)`, and putting that tag in UC killed the pose too. Raezuto: try `-0.5::lace pantyhose hooked on heel (meme)::` and tune the number. Gluttonous Beast settled on the meme in UC plus `-1::fabric pull::` in the prompt.

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, guidance 5, 23 steps. Base: `pov, 2girls, cafe table, window light, high complexity`. Box 1: `girl, female pov, pov hands, holding coffee cup, sleeves`. Box 2: `girl, sitting across, smiling, looking at viewer, short brown hair, cardigan`.

**CTA.** Try `armless` vs `-1::arms::` on one seed, and post the pair. Guide: §8 Community notes, Mon.

sections.title: A three-panel comic from one character box, and a V4.5 vibe stitched to a V5 panel
sections.lede: Two comic workflows from #nai-image-advice: one that puts the panel script inside a character box, and one that borrows a V4.5 vibe and extends it in V5.
sections.body:
**Panels in a box.** 司 PhazonMadness answered Benokelvin's "same character in every panel" question with a working cat-frog comic. The base prompt sets the layout in plain English: `3 panel comic. first panel is on top left. second panel is on top right. third panel is covering bottom center. forest, river, lily pads.` The character box holds the character once, then one line per panel: `Panel 1: on a lily pad.`, `Panel 2: jumping across one lily pad to another.`, `Panel 3: speech bubble saying "me-ribbit", facing viewer, on a lily pad.` The same text after a `|` in the base prompt also works if no boxes are open, but you lose the placement grid. Redwood Elf noticed the frog-cat lost its cat ears in panel 2, so expect a few rerolls.

**House note.** Our rule still stands: lettering goes through `text_overlays`, never typed. In Studio, put the bubble text in a `text_overlays` row targeting box 1 and keep the panel lines free of quoted text.

**V4.5 vibe + V5 panel.** ShameSoot's deer-gunslinger strip started as a V4.5 vibe-transfer gen. He expanded the canvas in V5 inpainting to add a second panel and the speech bubble, then resized to normal limits. "Basically, you can use v5 sort of if you use the original image as an inset reference." It's the same idea as Wednesday's reference-inset trick.

**Too many boxes.** He makes zombies gave V5 13 character prompts meant as a sequence. Instead of failing, it merged them into one anthology image. Glitterhoof's advice: get fewer panels working first, then add more.

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 28 steps, guidance 5, normal portrait. Base: `3 panel comic. first panel is on top left. second panel is on top right. third panel is covering bottom center. city park, autumn.` Box 1: `girl, short red hair, green scarf. panel 1: feeding pigeons. panel 2: pigeons flying away. panel 3: surprised, facing viewer.` Overlay: `{"text":"hey!","type":"speech","target":1}`.

**CTA.** Try 2 panels, then 3, then 4 on the same seed. Guide: §8 Community notes.

sections.title: This week's lab board: zero-weight order, Medium at 5 vs 8, six-girl positions
sections.lede: Five cheap A/Bs that would turn this weekend's staff answers into guide defaults. All free-tier, small sizes, fixed seeds.
sections.body:
1. **`0::` order.** `bear, 0::snow::` vs `0::snow::, bear`, three seeds, High 23 steps, guidance 5. Pass if B gets a white or polar look on 2 of 3. Then try `0::underwater::, girl, ...`.
2. **Medium guidance.** The same prompt on Medium at guidance 5 and 8 vs High at 5 and 8, two seeds. Check DarkTentacleMaster's claim that Medium tracks High at 5 and drifts at 8.
3. **Six-girl positions.** `6girls, group picture`, six one-line boxes, AI's choice vs custom positions, same seed. Count clones and missing characters.
4. **`armless` vs `-1::arms::`.** One character, `sleeveless dress`, same seed. Expect a missing limb vs hidden arms.
5. **UC as style on High.** UC empty vs `3d, realistic, glossy skin` vs prompt `-1::3d, realistic::`, same seed. Did the composition move?

**Settings unless noted:** V5 Full, small portrait, Euler Ancestral, guidance 5, rescale 0, quality tags on, Light UC (High only), HOUSE lowercase.

**CTA.** Lab results go to the Cellar plus `save_memory`. Medium rows append to `V5 Medium effort testing` (same name, never a new one), plus a lab article on this sheet.

sections.title: Behind the red wrapper: an anime-adaptation look in one sentence, turnarounds, and High vs Medium on skin
sections.lede: The unofficial guild was mostly showcase this weekend. Two threads had technique: getting a specific anime adaptation's look on V5, and High vs Medium on explicit gens.
sections.body:
**An anime adaptation's look on V5.** verif wanted the Spice and Wolf anime look, since V5 has no reference images yet. Raezuto: on V4.5 use `copyright:spice and wolf, official art`. On **V5, write it as a sentence**: `the composition is in the official animated art style of spice and wolf.` Add `anime coloring`, try **DPM++ 2M** for anime-screenshot gens, then `clean lineart` and `cel rendering`. For the 2008 series, pin the era with `year 2008` and push away from the reboot with `-1::year 2024::`. Raezuto finds **medium complexity** best for animated looks. Boxed Water adds similar artists at low weight (`0.3::artist::`), `-2.0::lowres, sketch::` in the positive prompt, and `high complexity, high depthness`. Result from verif: swapping to DPM++ 2M "made the most difference." Turning on furry mode brought it closer still (wolf ears), but per our house rule that's the `dataset_config` toggle, never typed.

**Multiple views.** ChiakiAsakira's `multiple views` wasn't working. Boxed Water: try `turnaround`, or `reference sheet` / `character profile`. thickwaifu found `character profile` also draws text that no negative removes. In Studio, check the Quality Tags `no text` sub-toggle before blaming the prompt.

**Hollow eyes.** For a jack-o'-lantern head with cut-out eyes: `empty eyes, eye socket` (Boxed Water).

**High vs Medium on skin.** Stealthybon's same-prompt pair (below): "Medium seems a lot smoother in a way, but in kinda the way tv anime is?" NTRender found High better in their tests. Gravel: "powered by medium effort, i don't see where the hate is coming from." thickwaifu noticed Medium doesn't use custom UC, which is now explained: Medium has no UC path at all.

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, DPM++ 2M, 23 steps, guidance 5: `the composition is in the official animated art style of a 2008 fantasy anime. 1girl, solo, wolf ears, long brown hair, medieval village, autumn, anime coloring, clean lineart, cel rendering, year 2008, medium complexity`.

**CTA.** A/B Euler Ancestral vs DPM++ 2M on that prompt, same seed. Guide: §8 Community notes (UNOFFICIAL).

sections.title: HOUSE: the shared Medium log, and two Studio gaps it turned up
sections.lede: Other Dreamscape MCP users have been appending Medium-vs-High pairs to one shared memory, `V5 Medium effort testing` (revision 25). Here's what it says, minus the rows we skip.
sections.body:
The log's default policy: **prefer Medium for V5 Full and switch to High only when Medium misses**, meaning missed tags or composition, lost detail, or a fix that needs UC. The weekend rows back that up, with three patterns:

- **Studio folds your negative prompt into `-1::` bans on Medium**, and the compiled UC is empty. Bans written that way worked: deck, glass and lattice banned put Tokyo Tower in the skyline instead of a second tower; a park table and foliage banned left a clean floor. A UC-only fix (an extra hand) never arrives on Medium. Even High with `extra hands` in the sent UC left a third hand on a railing once.
- **Medium smooths strain into a smile.** Pained, wincing or clenched faces came back as smiles on Medium in 3 of 3 rows, and High restored the wince. Two-hand interactions (two plush mittens pressed together) dropped on Medium and landed on High.
- **Wording traps.** `no head` cut a hole in a neck. `head out of frame` plus intact necks cropped at the chin. Naming one material per part (leather hat, glass eyes, minky hair) split materials on one plush. Satin and matte velvet still collapsed.

**Expand isn't the Drafting lock.** Expand metadata on Medium showed `v5_medium` at **28 steps, guidance 4.9, rescale 0.07**, compiled UC empty. That's different from the 14-step lock.

**Two Studio gaps worth a Menma look** (reported here, not filed):
1. Rentan lighting presets whose `!dg_` tokens compiled to **empty**: noon light stayed until `golden hour` / `city lights` were typed.
2. One row says `dataset_config.include ["furry"]` stayed selected in Studio but **injected nothing into the compiled prompt on either model**. Our documented toggle id is `"fur dataset"`, not `"furry"`, so this may just be the wrong id. Worth checking before the next pantry gen that relies on the toggle.

**Skipped:** one row about a character canonically under 18, and the maternity rows' body specifics. No new hip/WG/pregnancy recipe is claimed.

**CTA.** Cellar members testing Medium: append to the same memory name. Guide: §7 HOUSE Medium log.
